hints.title: Break an implication in the right way
hints.body: A counterexample to “if P, then Q” must make P true and Q false.
hints.recap: The condition and the failed conclusion must occur on the same object.
hints.pitfall: An object with a false premise cannot disprove this implication.
hints.pause: Apply that test to each card, using both sides of that card.

recall.reminder: Keep the assumption true while testing whether the conclusion can fail.

solution:
Card A has a vowel on the front and 3, an odd number, on the back. It makes the hypothesis true and the conclusion false.

Card E satisfies the claim; the consonant cards do not test its hypothesis. Answer A.
